messages:
maria: Hey team — customer TCK-4321 reporting intermittent 502s from hosted inference in eu1 when sending streaming requests with trailers. trace_id=abc123. They included a curl sample that shows a trailing header being sent and then an abrupt 502 from the edge. Can someone triage? :eyes:

kevin: Got the ticket. Any repro steps from customer? sample payload / approximate size?

maria: They say it happens for large streamed responses (~50-100MB total) and only when client uses Trailer headers (e.g. `Trailer: X-Sig`) and then sends a final trailer. They reproduced with their SDK, attached snippet: ```
curl -v --http2 \n  -H "Trailer: X-Checksum" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \n  --data-binary @big_payload.bin \n  "https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/hosts/guest/stream?model=xx-large"
```

ashley: Interesting. We've seen proxies drop trailers before when chunking/copying between layers. Any envoy/ingress logs from the time of abc123?

maria: Customer included bearer token and our edge trace header: `X-Trace: abc123`. They saw upstream respond OK but edge gave 502. Attached client-side tcpdump showing FIN after trailer.

infra-bot: alert: envoy upstream 502 response observed on frontdoor-eu1 cluster for trace abc123 (svc: edge-proxy-eu1).

kevin: Can someone enable debug for envoy on the node that handled abc123 and pull `error`/`warning` lines around that timestamp? I want to see if envoy dropped `TRAILER` frames or flagged `early response`/RST.

dan: Quick repro attempt from my laptop with a generated trailer reproduces a 502 locally against a staging frontdoor. Repro steps: ```
python -c "from http.client import HTTPConnection; conn=HTTPConnection('staging-edge:443'); conn.putrequest('POST','/v1/hosts/guest/stream'); conn.putheader('Trailer','X-Checksum'); conn.endheaders(); conn.send(b'--chunk1--'); conn.send(b'--chunk2--'); conn.send(b''); # send trailers here but envoy resets
```
Result: edge returned `502` and upstream got full body + trailer.

ashley: That suggests the upstream consumed the trailer but the edge ejected the stream afterwards. Could be our L7 proxy trying to coalesce trailers into headers and hitting a size/validation failure. Any recent changes to the l7 filter chain?

maria: We did flip a performance patch last week on frontdoor that toggles h2 window size + chunked buffer pooling (release 2026-03-10). Rollback candidate?

kevin: Before rolling back, let's collect: envoy logs, ingress nginx logs, and pcap on the frontdoor for the exact connection. Also grab per-request metrics from tracing: upstream latency, bytes_in, bytes_out, and any `local_reply` reasons.

sre-oncall: I'll capture tcpdump on 3 nodes that handled the hash-range for that time window and start a k8s port-forward for admin to dump envoy config. Command: `kubectl -n infra exec -it pod/frontdoor-xyz -- tcpdump -w /tmp/abc123.pcap tcp and port 443`

dan: For mitigation, customers can remove trailers or switch to putting checksum in final JSON chunk. For immediate customer workaround, suggest turning off `Trailer` header in their client SDK.

ashley: Ops note: we've seen a bug where envoy's `h2::decodeTrailers` path returns `Http::StreamReset` when trailer size > 8k after header coalescing. Not confirmed. Kevin pls confirm with debug logs.

kevin: On it, enabling `trace` level for `http2` and `connection` and will paste matching lines. If we find the `decoder_callbacks_->sendLocalReply` with `stream_reset`, we have the root.

infra-bot: job: started envoy debug logs collection (job id dbg-175001). ETA ~3m.

maria: Customer is on a paid SLA and asks for a short-term mitigation. I'll propose a configuration rule at the frontdoor to `strip: Trailer` for that tenant's route or route them to dedicated midproxy without the new perf patch. Any objections?

dan: Stripping trailers per-tenant sounds safe as a targeted mitigation. We need to ensure we don't break legitimate uses. Also add a polyfill note to client SDK.

sre-oncall: Collected pcap + envoy admin dump. Observed RST after END_STREAM from client and `upstream rstm: ECONNRESET` in the logs. Pasting excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T12:21:43.123Z] warning envoy http2: decodeTrailers(): oversized trailer detected, dropping stream
[2026-03-15T12:21:43.124Z] error envoy connection: stream reset by local, reason: STREAM_OVERFLOW
```

kevin: Bingo. `oversized trailer` log line confirms. Probable regression in chunked buffer pooling threshold introduced by the perf patch. I recommend rolling back the patch on eu1 frontdoor group and enabling per-tenant trailer-strip as fallback.

maria: I'll open an emergency change to rollback release 2026-03-10 on eu1 and apply `strip_trailers: true` on TCK-4321 route. Also filing follow-up to adjust buffer thresholds.

kevin: I'll coordinate the rollback and monitor 502 rate for that tenant. Monitor query: `sum(rate(edge.resp.5xx{region=\"eu1\",route=\"TCK-4321\"}[1m]))`

ashley: Add regression test for trailers to our staging e2e harness so this doesn't slip.

maria: Noted. I'll reply to the customer with the workaround and ETA for rollback (~20m). Assigning owner: dan for the strip rule + kevin for rollback.

dan: Assigned. I'll push the strip rule and verify with customer's repro.

kevin: Rollback started, watching logs. infra-bot will update when deployment finished.

infra-bot: deployment rollback complete for frontdoor-eu1 (rev 2026-03-09).

kevin: Post-rollback: 502s for abc123-type traces gone in last 10m. Metrics back to baseline.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update TCK-4321 with steps, timeline, and RCA pending. Follow-up: change request to widen trailer buffer limit and add e2e test. :white_check_mark:
